# VisionBridge

VisionBridge is a browser-based Indian Sign Language (ISL) A–Z isolated-letter recognition application with optional few-shot signer calibration.

## Application
- Sign in: https://visionbridge-2c7h.onrender.com/login
- Dashboard: https://visionbridge-2c7h.onrender.com/dashboard
- Live Translate: https://visionbridge-2c7h.onrender.com/translate
- Calibration: https://visionbridge-2c7h.onrender.com/calibration
- Letter History: https://visionbridge-2c7h.onrender.com/history
- Settings: https://visionbridge-2c7h.onrender.com/settings
- Speak prototype: https://visionbridge-2c7h.onrender.com/voice-to-sign
- Word Bank: https://visionbridge-2c7h.onrender.com/word-bank
- Personalization: https://visionbridge-2c7h.onrender.com/personalization

## Capabilities
- Browser camera hand tracking with MediaPipe
- A–Z isolated-letter recognition
- Optional few-shot signer calibration and adapter management
- Recognition history and CSV export
- Categorized vocabulary, custom phrases, and ten-slot Quick Access
- Personalization profiles, signing-speed preference, and speech-voice preference
- Browser speech recognition and sentence/token handling prototype

## Important scope limits
The validated ML task is single-frame A–Z letter classification. VisionBridge is not a validated full-sentence or semantic ISL translator. The Speak page is a prototype: the current word-sign and phrase-sign asset maps are empty, so do not describe it as playing animated semantic signs for arbitrary speech.

The current recorded model evaluation reports 4,633 prepared test samples, 98.273257% overall accuracy, 98.291294% macro class accuracy, and 78.770950% accuracy for W, the weakest class. These are stored dataset-evaluation results, not a real-world webcam guarantee. Signer-independent evaluation remains blocked because the dataset metadata does not expose verified signer IDs; this is a required release gate.

## Technical context
VisionBridge uses React, TypeScript, Vite, React Router, FastAPI, PyTorch, MediaPipe Tasks Hand Landmarker 0.10.35, and a 126-dimensional two-hand landmark pipeline.

## Access and validation
Most application routes require authentication. Camera access requires browser permission and HTTPS on deployed sites. CI does not replace physical-device camera/microphone or complete production end-to-end testing.
